high.title: IPCA, IGP-10: What to Expect from the Brazilian Economy Amid Escalating Middle East Conflict
high.summary:
Brazilian inflation indicators are showing concerning deterioration due to escalating Middle East conflict. The IGP-10 index jumped to 2.94% in April versus -0.24% in March, driven primarily by surging oil prices. The weekly Focus Bulletin has revised IPCA inflation expectations for 2026 upward to 4.71%, while maintaining projections for the Selic rate at 12.50% for the year, signaling an extended period of high interest rates.

The oil price surge is creating broad-based inflationary pressures across the entire production chain - from transportation and logistics to food prices and agricultural fertilizers. This comprehensive impact threatens to push inflation well above the central bank's target range. For BRL traders, this creates a challenging environment where higher inflation may force the BCB to maintain restrictive monetary policy longer than previously expected. Bond investors should prepare for potential yield increases as inflation expectations deteriorate, while the prolonged high-rate environment could weigh on equity valuations despite supporting the currency in the near term.

medium.title: Ana Paula, Milena, Juliano Floss: Who Will Profit in Conservative Fixed Income with Selic at 14.75% with BBB 26's R$ 5.4 Million Prize?
medium.summary: The article discusses Big Brother Brasil contestants and the recent Selic rate cut from 15% to 14.75% by COPOM last month. Despite the rate reduction, Brazilian fixed income remains the most attractive asset class currently. The piece highlights how conservative fixed income investments continue to offer compelling returns even after the modest rate cut, reflecting the still-restrictive monetary policy stance.

medium.title: Bradesco (BBDC4) Buys Remaining Stake of Banco BV in Tivio Capital
medium.summary: Bradesco completed the acquisition of Banco BV's remaining stake in asset manager Tivio Capital, consolidating full ownership of the alternative investment platform. This strategic move aims to expand sophisticated investment products for clients beyond traditional market risk. Tivio will continue operating independently with its own governance structure, strengthening Bradesco's alternative investment capabilities in line with global trends.
